No. After Benjamini-Hochberg FDR correction for multiple testing, none of the 16 pairwise Spearman correlations between the 4 circulating immune-cell populations (CCR7+ CD11b+ CD27- B cells, Conventional DC, HLA-DR+ Non-Naive CD4 T Cells, HLA-DR+ Non-Naive CD8 T Cells) and the 4 serum proteins (CXCL10, CXCL9, IFN-gamma, Soluble PD-1) reached statistical significance (FDR q < 0.05) at the C2D1 on-treatment timepoint in the PRINCE trial (PICI0002), either in the pooled cohort (n = 65-73) or within any of the three treatment arms (Nivolumab+Chemo n=23, APX005M+Chemo n=24, Nivolumab+APX005M+Chemo n=26).

The strongest nominal trends (raw p < 0.10, none surviving FDR) were:
- Pooled: CCR7+ CD11b+ CD27- B cells with CXCL9 (rho = -0.233, raw p = 0.062, q = 0.535) and with CXCL10 (rho = -0.222, raw p = 0.076, q = 0.535).
- Nivolumab+APX005M+Chemo arm: HLA-DR+ Non-Naive CD4 T Cells with IFN-gamma (rho = -0.588, raw p = 0.005, q = 0.080) and with CXCL9 (rho = -0.460, raw p = 0.036, q = 0.235).
- APX005M+Chemo arm: CCR7+ CD11b+ CD27- B cells with CXCL10 (rho = -0.432, raw p = 0.050, q = 0.436).

These nominal trends are directionally consistent with known biology (IFN-gamma pathway induction of CXCL9/CXCL10 and T-cell chemotaxis), but this dataset (4 cell populations x 4 proteins, n = 21-26 per arm) is underpowered to confirm correlations at FDR-corrected significance. Per-arm subgroup sizes provide 80% power only for |rho| > 0.55-0.60. The analysis cannot exclude modest but biologically meaningful correlations. Independent replication with the full CyTOF and Olink panels in a larger cohort at this timepoint is warranted.
